newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Crimea region sacks parliament leader.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Crimea region sacks parliament leader.

text.p: Parliament in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula dismissed its speaker on Thursday, fuelling political tensions in the pro-Russian region.
Deputies voted 58 to one to sack Vasily Kiselyov, a pragmatic former collective farm boss who backs closer economic ties with Russia but rules out separation from Ukraine.

The region of 2.7 million people was part of Russia for nearly two centuries until the Kremlin gave it to Ukraine, then a Soviet republic, as a "gift" in 1954. Two-thirds of the population are ethnic Russians.
"This parliament is a destructive force," Kiselyov told a news conference after the vote. "The situation in Crimea is getting to the point where the Ukrainian parliament will impose order here."
Parliament in Crimea has already voted to reorganise the government and to oust local Prime Minister Arkady Demidenko, who has pledged to stay in office.
But Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma said the Crimean deputies were violating the constitution by taking such a step.
